findings.baseline_deterministic: A1 and A2 (schedule OFF) have identical control_end SIM 126.26 s and fine alignment 28.40 s; synchronous mode is reproducible and load-insensitive.
findings.sync_vs_realtime: Synchronous fine alignment 28.4 SIM s vs 51-78 SIM s in realtime runs: realtime decision latency, not only controller gain, dominates fine-stage time.
b1_failure_mechanism: Forward stage (slot r1 = physical r3 via pair binding): scheduled commands .15 reduced image error .186 -> .026 in 6 slices (A1 needed ~26 slices to reach .054).
Carry-over motion from the preceding .139/.15 commands overshot the target to -0.0062 (outer tolerance .004). The no-crossing cap used only the current command, not residual motion.

Beyond the target the pose estimate is not monotonic: post-run referee (evaluation only) shows physical r3 advancing ~6 cm while the image-derived error went from negative back to +.016, so the model kept commanding forward until RGB left learned support at SIM 34.0.
No beam contact, beam displacement, weld or obstacle contact in B1.
findings.claims: No speed or success claim for the v31 schedule; it is unsafe as designed because overshoot enters a region where the pose model is not trustworthy.

next_design: Overshoot-proof variant: limit predicted travel including residual motion from the previous slice, hand back to the unchanged controller well before the target, and disable the schedule for the rest of a stage after any sign flip. Validate offline on B1/A1 traces before a new protocol.
